forecast-period.text: A high pressure system centred over the Tasman Sea extends a ridge over SA ahead of a low pressure trough that is expected to move over the far west of SA during Wednesday. The trough will slip southeastwards over southern coasts during Thursday and Friday, before being confined to the west over the weekend.
For latest warnings go to www.bom.gov.au, subscribe to RSS feeds, call 1300 659 210* or listen for warnings on relevant TV and radio broadcasts.
* Calls to 1300 numbers cost around 27.5c incl. GST, higher from mobiles or public phones.

Cold at first about eastern districts with with patchy frost. Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms developing in the far southwest and in the far northeast corner. Maximum temperatures above average, grading to well above average in the west. Southeast to northeasterly winds ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change in the southwest during the afternoon.
Dry and mostly clear. Southeast to northeasterly winds. Afternoon sea breezes near the coast.

Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far southwest and the chance of an isolated shower about southern coasts. Maximum temperatures well above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds ahead of a southwest to southeasterly change in the west.

Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far southwest and the chance of an isolated shower about southern coasts. Maximum temperatures well above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending fresh at times in the north, tending southwest to southeasterly change about western and southern districts.

text.p: Isolated showers and possible thunderstorms in the far west and the chance of an isolated shower about southern coasts. Maximum temperatures well above average. Northeast to northwesterly winds, tending fresh at times in the north, tending southwest to southeasterly about western and southern parts.

Cumulative rainfall totals to the end of Saturday: Generally less than 2 mm about western parts and southern coasts, with local falls of 2 to 10 mm possible about the far southwest and southern coasts of the Lower South East and Kangaroo Island.
